intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that ichthyosis with erythrokeratoderma (IEKD) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the KLK11 gene.

checks.claim: Ichthyosis with erythrokeratoderma (IEKD) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the KLK11 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We provide evidence that variants at Gly50 affecting the SP cleavage of KLK11 cause a new autosomal-dominant cornification disorder with abnormal desquamation.
checks.explanation: Heterozygous Gly50 variants in KLK11 cause the disorder; the disease name IEKD is the draft's label.

paragraphs.text: Ichthyosis with erythrokeratoderma is an autosomal dominant Mendelian disorder of cornification characterized by early-onset ichthyosiform erythroderma or erythrokeratoderma, with abnormal skin desquamation and a thickened, dense stratum corneum (Gong et al., 2023). Large truncal hyperkeratotic pigmented plaques have also been described (Takeichi et al., 2023).

paragraphs.text: Gong et al. (2023) studied 3 families with a previously undescribed cornification disorder, comprising a familial case and 2 sporadic cases. The disorder was characterized by early-onset ichthyosiform erythroderma or erythrokeratoderma. The patients showed a thickened, dense stratum corneum, indicating abnormal skin desquamation.

paragraphs.text: By whole-exome sequencing in 3 families with ichthyosis with erythrokeratoderma, including a familial case and 2 sporadic cases, Gong et al. (2023) identified 2 heterozygous variants affecting gly50 in the KLK11 gene, located around the signal peptide cleavage site of this kallikrein-related peptidase; one was a c.149G-A transition resulting in a gly50-to-glu (G50E) substitution. In vitro experiments in eukaryotic overexpression systems showed that the variants perturbed signal peptide cleavage of KLK11, leading to subcellular mislocalization and impaired extracellular secretion of the G50E variant.

paragraphs.text: Gong et al. (2023) noted that KLK11 belongs to the family of kallikrein-related peptidases that participate in skin desquamation by decomposing corneodesmosomes, a process essential for shedding of the stratum corneum. In stratum corneum samples from patients with KLK11 variants, both trypsin-like and chymotrypsin-like proteolytic activities were significantly decreased, and reduced proteolysis of desmoglein-1 and delayed degeneration of corneodesmosomes were detected, indicating delayed skin desquamation.

paragraphs.text: In patients with ichthyosis with erythrokeratoderma, Gong et al. (2023) identified a heterozygous c.149G-A transition in the KLK11 gene, resulting in a gly50-to-glu (G50E) substitution near the signal peptide cleavage site. In vitro, the variant perturbed signal peptide cleavage, leading to subcellular mislocalization and impaired extracellular secretion of KLK11. Mice homozygous for the equivalent Klk11 variant (c.131G-A, G44E) showed hyperkeratosis and abnormal desquamation.

agent.process_note: I read both files in full. Gong et al. (2023) is available as an abstract only, and Takeichi et al. (2023) as a title only. The abstract names one variant, KLK11 c.149G>A (p.Gly50Glu). It does not name the second variant affecting Gly50, and it gives no ancestry, consanguinity, ages or per-family genotypes, so those are left out. No HGNC reference data were supplied, so the intro gives no KLK11 MIM number or chromosome location. The Takeichi paper is used only for what its title states.
